To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

species richness of both mosses and vascular flora increases towards the equator and is positively correlated only in near equator zone, and the relations with some factors are different for both plant groups.
the relations between species richness and environmental factors differ between moss and vascular plant species at a global scale.
species richness of vascular plant and mosses are significantly positively correlated, but only in the near-equator zone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
global biodiversity gradients, which are the most important factors in conservation policy.
the global patterns of plant species diversity.
the global patterns of moss and vascular plant richness and the factors influencing these patterns.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the global patterns of vascular plant and moss diversity are similar, but not identical.
there are some similarities in the trends between moss and vascular plant diversites, but also differences.
there are global gradients in species richness for both mosses and vascular vegetation, but these gradients differ in the magnitude and direction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the global distribution of vascular plants and mosses is different.
the global gradients of species richness of different taxon group are not the same, and the relations of different factors with species richness differ with distance from equator.
global patterns of moss diversity are not as well understood as those of vascular plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
conservation of biodiversity is a complex task, and it requires consideration of all diversity factors and their interactions.
the global patterns of species diversity of mosses and of vascular plants are not identical and that conservation strategies should consider the differences.

the relations between species richness and environmental factors of different plant groups are not the same, and therefore, the global conservation of biodiversity requires a more complex understanding of the drivers of diversity of various plant groups.
